sanctionedSuppressions.reason: Equivalent mutant, proof at the site: a heavy OUTER layer has no lower bound (nothing goes over it), so estimateTempRange drops this floor before returning and no input can distinguish -4 from +4. Hoisted to a named constant because a Stryker directive cannot attach inside an object literal.

Equivalent mutant, proof at the site: removing the undefined-weight guard changes no behaviour, because an undefined weight indexes every table to undefined and the next guard returns the same thing. It is load-bearing for the compiler, not the runtime — without it `Weight | undefined` cannot index `Record<Weight, Band>`.

Unreachable, proof at the site: `runHourKeys` always yields at least the starting hour, so destructuring it can never give undefined. The guard exists because the compiler types `keys[0]` as `CacheKey | undefined` whatever the runtime does, which is also why its return value is unobservable.

Equivalent mutant, proof at the site: an empty `inArray` matches nothing, so the two queries below the early return produce the same zeros either way. What the return saves is those two queries, on a cron that fires every hour.

Equivalent mutant, proof at the site: hour 0 is known to be a cache miss, because resolveAndAttach looked it up and returned early if it hit. Widening the guard only adds a lookup that always misses — a billed query, which is why the guard stays and why no test can distinguish it.

Equivalent mutant, proof at the site: the result map is filled by a loop over `keyed`, so returning early on an empty one changes no answer. It saves a query that would otherwise scan every non-manual observation.

Equivalent mutant, proof at the site: emptying the cell-condition callback widens the WHERE to every non-manual row, and the rows are looked up by cell key afterwards — so the answer is identical and only the scan grows.

Unreachable, proof at the site: the insert either wrote the row or conflicted with one already present, so the read that follows always finds something. The guard exists to narrow `ObservationRow | undefined` for the caller.

Equivalent mutant, proof at the site: the probe key is arbitrary. The check asks R2 whether an object exists, and a miss is a successful round trip — which is the whole point. Any string, empty included, proves the same reachability, so no assertion can tell them apart.

Unreachable, proof at the site: `insertThenRead` inserts and then reads back the same identity, and the insert either wrote the row or conflicted with one already there — so the read always finds something. The guard narrows `Row | undefined` for the caller and nothing else.

Equivalent mutant, proof at the site: emptying an onConflict target leaves a bare ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING, which swallows the same collision and every other one too. Naming the index says which collision is expected; no query can tell the two apart. Hoisted to named constants because a directive cannot attach to an object literal mid-chain.
Equivalent mutant, proof at the site: an empty `inArray` matches nothing, so the defaults map comes back empty either way. The early return saves the query.

Unreachable fallback, proof at the site: `count()` always answers with exactly one row. The optional chain is there because `noUncheckedIndexedAccess` types `rows[0]` as possibly undefined, which is the compiler being right about arrays in general rather than about this query.
